sections.skill: Calculate credit card interest using the daily periodic rate and the average daily balance

questions.prompt: A card has a 21.9% APR. What is the daily periodic rate (APR ÷ 365) as a percent?
questions.intro: Most credit cards charge interest using a daily periodic rate (DPR): DPR = APR ÷ 365. Interest for a billing cycle ≈ average daily balance × DPR × number of days in the cycle.
questions.topic: How credit card interest is calculated
sources: CFPB (Credit CARD Act / Regulation Z): Card issuers must mail statements at least 21 days before the due date; statements show the minimum payment warning; applicants under 21 need independent income or a cosigner. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/credit-cards/answers/key-terms/)

questions.prompt: In a 30-day cycle, a card balance is $500 for 10 days, $800 for 10 days (after a $300 purchase), and $600 for 10 days (after a $200 payment). What is the average daily balance?
questions.intro: The average daily balance (ADB) is the sum of each day's balance divided by the number of days in the cycle. When balances last different numbers of days, weight each balance by its days.
questions.topic: How credit card interest is calculated

misconceptions.C: Averages the three balances as if weighted equally by events

sources: CFPB (Credit CARD Act / Regulation Z): Card issuers must mail statements at least 21 days before the due date; statements show the minimum payment warning; applicants under 21 need independent income or a cosigner. questions.prompt: Using an average daily balance of $633.33, a 21.9% APR, and a 30-day cycle, what is the interest charge (nearest cent)?
questions.intro: Interest for a billing cycle = average daily balance × (APR ÷ 365) × days in the cycle.
questions.topic: How credit card interest is calculated

misconceptions.D: Uses the full APR for a month

questions.prompt: How would making the $200 payment on day 11 instead of day 21 change that cycle's interest?

choices.text: Lower it, because the balance is lower for more days
Raise it, because payments add interest
No change at all, because only the ending balance matters

questions.correct_answer: Lower it, because the balance is lower for more days
questions.intro: With the average daily balance method, the balance on every day of the cycle counts, so timing of payments and purchases matters.
questions.feedback: An earlier payment lowers the balance for more days, lowering the ADB and the interest.

sections.relationship: Average daily balance is a weighted average; students who average only the listed balances get it wrong.

questions.prompt: A balance is $100 for 20 days and $400 for 10 days. Which calculation gives the average daily balance over 30 days?
questions.intro: A weighted average multiplies each value by how long it lasts, adds, then divides by the total time.

questions.prompt: What is the average daily balance in that example (a balance of $100 for 20 days and $400 for 10 days)?

sections.skill: Interest on a carried balance, month after month

questions.prompt: Ivy carries $1,000 at 24% APR and makes no payments or purchases. About how much interest is added after one month (APR ÷ 12)?
questions.intro: When a balance is carried and not paid, interest is added to the balance, and next month interest is charged on the larger balance (compounding).

sections.skill: How payments are applied to different APRs

questions.prompt: A card has $1,000 at a 0% promotional APR and $500 at a 22% purchase APR. Ella pays $300, of which $40 is the minimum. Under federal rules, where must the amount ABOVE the minimum go?
questions.intro: When a card has balances with different APRs, the Credit CARD Act requires issuers to apply payments above the minimum to the balance with the highest APR first. The minimum itself can be applied however the issuer chooses.
questions.feedback: The $260 above the minimum goes to the higher-APR balance first.
questions.topic: How credit card interest is calculated
sources: CFPB (Credit CARD Act / Regulation Z): Card issuers must mail statements at least 21 days before the due date; statements show the minimum payment warning; applicants under 21 need independent income or a cosigner. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/credit-cards/answers/key-terms/)

questions.prompt: Under that rule, how much of Ella's $300 payment (minimum $40) goes toward the 22% balance at least?
questions.intro: Payments above the minimum must be applied to the highest-APR balance first.
questions.feedback: $300 − $40 = $260 must go to the highest-APR balance.
